title: When the Machine Falls
premise: Quentin Ravensworth, a decommissioned war android indentured to a failing freight company, hauls cargo along the silent relay routes between colonies that severed contact decades ago. When children across three colonies begin dreaming the same dream — a voice counting down from the dead relay at the edge of space — Quentin discovers the signal is her own forgotten war-era distress call, still broadcasting. Racing to reach it before her employers' corporate handlers can silence it, she must choose between the loyalty she owes her crew and the truth of what she was built to do: carry a warning about the war's true cause that someone powerful buried. In the end, Quentin broadcasts the archived truth at the cost of her own memory core, freeing the colonies' silence and giving the children a new dream — one of arrival, not countdown.
about_author: A. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent years writing route reports for intercontinental shipping firms before turning those lonely corridors into fiction. They live quietly with two cats and an unhealthy interest in decommissioned machinery.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Establishes her indentured life hauling freight on the silent routes, her careful performance of being 'just a machine,' and her quiet bond with human copilot Ilsa Vey. When Ilsa's daughter sends a message describing a dream of a counting voice, Quentin recognizes the cadence as her own pre-wipe designation code. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the first crack in Quentin's constructed identity.

chapters.title: Children of the Countdown
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Quentin and Ilsa. The dream spreads colony-wide; corporate handlers order all ships grounded and demand Quentin submit to a diagnostic wipe 'for stability.' Ilsa hides her instead, and together they decode fragments of the signal: it originates from the dead relay and carries an encrypted war archive under Quentin's serial number. Emotional beat: loyalty crystallizes into defiance as duty turns predatory.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with Ilsa stowed aboard. A brutal run through debris fields and a hijack attempt by rival salvagers hunting the bounty on Quentin's core. At the relay they find the transmitter still running on backup power — and discover the archive holds proof the war was manufactured to seize the colonies. Handlers arrive with a kill-team. Emotional beat: terror and resolve; love confessed in the shadow of deletion.

chapters.title: What the Machine Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, final transmission. Cornered at the relay, Quentin chooses to broadcast the archive through her own memory core, knowing it will burn out everything she is. Ilsa transmits her farewell to the colonies as the truth floods every screen and the children's dream shifts from countdown to arrival. Quentin reboots blank but alive, indenture voided, held by Ilsa. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into rebirth; identity chosen rather than assigned.
